newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee closes above lows as NY recovers.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee closes above lows as NY recovers.

text.p: LIFFE coffee futures erased some early losses on Tuesday on industry buying and a recovery in New York but prices still ended lower on overhead origin selling.
Prices made their way sharply lower at the start in line with opening calls of $25 lower on the back of a slide in New York on Monday.
All eyes focused on New York's spot December expiry later with traders watching if the contract goes off the board with more than 10 cents premium over March.
By 1720 GMT, the Dec/March premium held at around 16 cents. The premium has been hovering at a high level on tightness of spot deliverable coffee.
The tight situation is expected to remain for some time.
By the close, London's second-position March stood $17 down at $1,258 a tonne after a session's low of $1,245 while front-month January eased $14 at $1,314.
Jan/March switch was active and accounted for most of the day's total volume of 5,046 lots.
Traders kept a close watch on reports of a cold airmass which some forecasters said could cause freezing temperatures and possible damage to the Mexican coffee belt later this week.
"There was a big frost four or five years ago around Christmas time which did a significant amount of damage to the Mexican crop," said one.
"It (the frost) is always a threat...I think it's become much more of a possibility in recent years because the climate has changed a little bit," he said.
"But it doesn't look like there will be a frost as far south as the coffee areas. But things changed very quickly," he added.
